messages:
jordan: Hey team, customer 'Acme Health' reporting mass failures when calling KMS in their Private deployment after a maintenance window. Errors started ~17:05 UTC. They see decryption failures and 403s from the vendor HSM backend. Requesting urgent help — customer impact: production traffic dropped ~40%.

maria: Can you paste the exact error payloads/log lines? Also confirm whether staging and prod share the same egress path.

jordan: Pasted below from the Redwood proxy logs (prod):
```
2026-03-17T16:58:12Z ERROR kms-connector: decrypt request id=abc123 remote=10.0.5.12:443 status=403 body="Forbidden: source_ip not in allowlist"
2026-03-17T16:58:12Z DEBUG http: upstream_response_time=0.112
```
Customer app logs show: `KMSError: forbidden (403) - key access denied`

kevin: That 403 string looks like the vendor HSM is IP-allowlisting our SNAT IP. Did the customer or we change NAT/Egress IPs during the window? Any recent infra change notes?

jordan: Customer's network team applied a routing change to funnel egress through a shared NAT pool (elastic IPs changed). They said new EIPs were assigned at 16:45 UTC.

maria: OK. Quick repro commands I asked them to run — they ran dig and curl from a prod box: 
```
# from prod instance
$ dig +short kms.acme-hsm.internal
54.23.12.9
$ curl -v https://kms.acme-hsm.internal/v1/decrypt -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." --cert client.pem --key client.key
* Connected to 54.23.12.9 (54.23.12.9) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection to 54.23.12.9 failed: HTTP code 403
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{ "message": "source_ip not in allowlist" }
```
Note: staging boxes still route via old EIP and succeed.

samantha: Customer ops confirms they had previously registered the old EIP block with the HSM vendor. They didn't realize the NAT change would flip IPs.

kevin: That would explain why staging (old EIP) works and prod (new EIP) doesn't. Root cause looks like vendor-side allowlist mismatch. Two remediation options: 1) Customer requests vendor to add the new EIP(s) to their allowlist; 2) Customer pins prod to a stable EIP (restore previous NAT or allocate dedicated NAT EIP) so vendor allowlist remains valid.

maria: Also asked them to run an http traceroute/conn to show source IP seen by vendor (they ran tcpdump and shared):
```
17:01:02.123 IP 10.0.5.12.443 > 54.23.12.9.443: Flags [S], seq 0
# vendor side logs (redacted): incoming_conn from 3.120.45.9 -> rejected by allowlist
```
So vendor saw 3.120.45.9 which matches the new NAT EIP.

jordan: Customer has opened a ticket with the HSM vendor and asked us for a temporary mitigation. Any short-term fixes we can suggest that don't require vendor changes?

kevin: Short-term: if they're able, restore the previous NAT EIP or create a one-to-one EIP for the Redwood private deployment's NAT gateway. That preserves the old source IP. Otherwise vendor needs to add the new EIP. We can't change vendor allowlist.

maria: Also flagged that some customers try to work around with DNS -> PrivateLink or VPC peering, but that requires vendor support. I suggested they request vendor to support adding the private-hosted-zone entry + PrivateLink or accept a CIDR rather than a single IP.

samantha: Customer applied a temporary rollback to the previous NAT assignment at 17:12 UTC — they report KMS calls are back to green. Monitoring shows 1 minute to full recovery.

ops-bot: incident-note: incident 2026-03-17-KMS-ALLOWLIST resolved as of 17:13 UTC (root cause: SNAT EIP change caused vendor-side IP allowlist rejection).

jordan: Closing loop: root cause confirmed — change to egress/source IP was not communicated to HSM vendor and vendor uses strict IP allowlist. Action items for customer: 1) get vendor to add new EIPs OR 2) reserve stable EIP for prod NAT; for us: document guidance in Private deployment runbook about communicating NAT/EIP changes to KMS/HSM vendors and include a checklist for egress allowlist updates.

maria: Adding runbook task: "Validate KMS vendor allowlist when changing NAT/EIP" and a snippet showing how to verify from host: `curl https://ifconfig.me` to confirm outbound IP.

kevin: Marking thread resolved in support and shared remediation template with customer ops.

samantha: Customer confirmed vendor added a note to their onboarding docs to accept CIDR ranges to avoid this in future. :white_check_mark:
